docs.title: Welcome to the AD4x4 API
docs.text: This documentation provides a comprehensive overview of the AD4x4 API, covering everything you need to know to get started. The API is designed to be easy to use and follows standard REST conventions.

docs.title: Main Resources
docs.text:
The AD4x4 API is organized around a few main resources:

  • Authentication and Profiles: Manage user accounts, profiles, and authentication.
  • Trips: Create, manage, and view off-road trips.
  • Meeting Points: Define and manage meeting points for trips.
  • Upgrade Requests: Handle requests for user account upgrades.
  • Account Deletion: Manage the account deletion process.
  • Notifications: Configure and manage user notifications.
  • UI Strings: Retrieve and manage editable UI strings for the client applications.
  • Permissions System: Control user access to different parts of the API.

docs.title: Account Deletion
docs.text: This document explains how a user can request the deletion of their account.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The account deletion process is designed to be simple and secure. It involves two main steps:

  1. The user makes an API request to signal their intent to delete their account.
  2. A background process runs periodically, and after a 3-day grace period, it anonymizes the user's data.

This grace period allows for a "cooling off" period, during which the user can change their mind. The anonymization process ensures that all personally identifiable information is removed from the user's profile, while preserving the integrity of any content they may have created (e.g., trip comments).

docs.title: API Endpoint
docs.text:
To initiate the account deletion process, the client must make a POST request to the following endpoint:

POST /api/members/request-deletion

This endpoint does not require any request body. The authenticated user associated with the request will be marked for deletion.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Success

A successful request will return a 200 OK status code and a JSON body indicating success:

{
    "success": true
}

Error: Deletion Request Already Exists

If the user has already requested deletion and a request is pending, the API will return a 400 Bad Request status code and the following JSON error message:

{
    "success": false,
    "message": "deletion_request_already_exists"
}

docs.title: Anonymization Details
docs.text:
After the 3-day grace period, the user's account will be anonymized. This is a permanent and irreversible action. The following fields will be changed:

  • The user will be marked as inactive.
  • The username will be replaced with a randomly generated string (e.g., deleted_user_...).
  • The email address will be changed to a dummy address (e.g., ...@deleted.com).
  • The first name will be set to "Anonymous".
  • The last name will be cleared.

docs.title: API Concepts
docs.text: This document covers high-level concepts for interacting with the AD4x4 API.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The API uses JWT (JSON Web Token) authentication. To authenticate:

  1. Obtain Token: POST to /api/token/ with username and password
  2. Use Token: Include in Authorization header as Bearer <token>
  3. Refresh Token: POST to /api/token/refresh/ with refresh token

docs.title: Authentication Header Format
docs.text: Authorization: Bearer <your_jwt_token>

docs.title: Obtain Token Pair
docs.text:
• Endpoint: POST /api/token/
  • Body: json { "username": "your_username", "password": "your_password" }
  • Response: json { "access": "eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGc...", "refresh": "eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGc..." }

docs.title: Refresh Token
docs.text:
• Endpoint: POST /api/token/refresh/
  • Body: json { "refresh": "eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGc..." }
  • Response: json { "access": "eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGc..." }

docs.title: Response Format
docs.text: Most endpoints return responses in the following formats:

docs.title: Success Response (Unified)
docs.text:
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "operation_successful"
}

docs.title: Error Response (Unified)
docs.text:
{
  "success": false,
  "message": "error_description"
}

docs.title: List Response (Paginated)
docs.text:
{
  "count": 100,
  "next": "http://api.example.org/api/items/?page=3",
  "previous": "http://api.example.org/api/items/?page=1",
  "results": []
}

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: The API uses standard HTTP status codes and returns detailed error messages.

docs.title: 400 Bad Request
docs.text:
{
  "success": false,
  "message": {
    "field_name": [
      "This field is required."
    ],
    "another_field": [
      "Invalid value."
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: 401 Unauthorized
docs.text:
{
  "detail": "Authentication credentials were not provided."
}

or

{
  "detail": "Given token not valid for any token type"
}

docs.title: 403 Forbidden
docs.text:
{
  "success": false,
  "message": "no_permission_to_perform_action"
}

docs.title: 404 Not Found
docs.text:
{
  "detail": "Not found."
}

docs.title: 422 Unprocessable Entity
docs.text:
{
  "success": false,
  "message": "waitlist_enforced_globally"
}

docs.title: 500 Internal Server Error
docs.text:
{
  "error": "An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later."
}

docs.title: File Uploads
docs.text: Endpoints that accept file uploads (images, track files, etc.) use multipart/form-data encoding.

docs.title: Example: Upload Trip Image
docs.text:
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8000/api/trips/456/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN" \
  -F "image=@/path/to/image.jpg" \
  -F "title=Updated Trip Title"

docs.title: Supported File Types
docs.text:
• Images: JPEG, PNG, GIF
  • Track Files: GPX, KML
  • Documents: PDF (for certain endpoints)

docs.title: File Size Limits
docs.text:
• Profile avatars: 5MB
  • Car images: 5MB
  • Trip images: 10MB
  • Track files: 2MB

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Always use HTTPS in production
  2. Store JWT tokens securely (not in localStorage for web apps)
  3. Refresh tokens before they expire
  4. Handle token expiration gracefully
  5. Use pagination for large datasets
  6. Implement proper error handling
  7. Validate data on the client side before sending
  8. Use appropriate HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE)
  9. Include proper Content-Type headers
  10. Test with the Swagger UI at /docs/swagger-ui/

docs.title: Authentication and Profiles
docs.text:
This document outlines the API endpoints for user authentication, registration, and profile management.

For a high-level overview of the authentication process, please refer to the API Concepts document.

docs.title: Registration and Password Management
docs.text: The API provides endpoints for user registration and password management, powered by the rest_registration library.

docs.title: Registration
docs.text:
POST /api/auth/register/

The request body should include the user's details. Refer to the MemberRegistrationSerializer for the full list of required and optional fields.

docs.title: Change Password
docs.text:
Authenticated users can change their password by making a POST request to /api/auth/change-password/.

POST /api/auth/change-password/

Request Body:

{
    "old_password": "current_password",
    "password": "new_password",
    "password2": "new_password_confirmation"
}

Note: password and password2 must match.

docs.title: Other Endpoints
docs.text:
The rest_registration library also provides endpoints for: * Resetting a forgotten password * Verifying registration via email

Please refer to the library's documentation for details on these flows.

docs.title: Retrieving a Profile
docs.text:
To retrieve a user's profile, make a GET request to /api/members/{id}/.

GET /api/members/{id}/

Success Response: The response will be a JSON object containing the user's profile information. The fields returned are defined by the ProfileSerializer.

Note: While the serializer and database use snake_case for field names (e.g., first_name), the API will return camelCase in the response body (e.g., firstName).

{
    "id": 1,
    "username": "testuser",
    "email": "test@example.com",
    "firstName": "Test",
    "lastName": "User",
    "phone": "1234567890",
    "carBrand": "Toyota",
    "carModel": "Land Cruiser",
    "carYear": 2022,
    "carColor": "White",
    "carImage": null,
    "dob": "2000-01-01",
    "iceName": "Jane Doe",
    "icePhone": "0987654321",
    "level": {
        "id": 1,
        "name": "Newbie"
    },
    "tripCount": 5,
    "avatar": null,
    "permissions": [...],
    "paidMember": true,
    "dateJoined": "2023-01-01T12:00:00Z",
    "city": "Dubai",
    "gender": "M",
    "nationality": "AE",
    "title": ""
}

docs.title: Updating a Profile
docs.text:
To update a user's profile, make a PATCH request to /api/members/{id}/. Users can only update their own profiles unless they are an administrator.

PATCH /api/members/{id}/

Request Body: The request body should contain the fields to be updated. For a list of editable fields, refer to the EditMemberSerializer. Note that some fields like username, email, and level are read-only.

Success Response: A successful update will return a 200 OK status code and the updated profile data.

docs.title: Editable Strings (UIString) API
docs.text: This document outlines how to use the Editable Strings (UIString) API to manage translations for the application.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The UIString feature allows for dynamic management of strings in the application's UI. Strings are stored as key-value pairs, with support for English and Arabic translations. The API provides endpoints for creating, retrieving, updating, and deleting these strings.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: All API endpoints require authentication. You must have the EDIT_UI_STRINGS permission to create, update, or delete UI strings.

docs.title: Retrieve a UI String
docs.text:
• GET /api/strings/{key}/

    Retrieves a single UI string by its key.

    Parameters:

    • key (string): The key of the UI string to retrieve.
    • lang (string, optional): The language to retrieve. Can be en or ar. Defaults to en.

    Example Request:

    bash curl -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/?lang=ar"

    Example Response:

    json { "key": "welcome_message", "values": { "title": "مرحباً", "body": "مرحباً بك في تطبيقنا!" } }

docs.title: Create a UI String
docs.text:
• POST /api/strings/

    Creates a new UI string.

    Example Request:

    bash curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "key": "new_feature_announcement", "values_en": { "title": "New Feature!", "description": "We have a new feature for you to try." }, "values_ar": { "title": "ميزة جديدة!", "description": "لدينا ميزة جديدة لتجربتها." } }' "https://example.com/api/strings/"

docs.title: Update a UI String
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/strings/{key}/

    Updates an existing UI string.

    Example Request (PUT):

    bash curl -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "key": "welcome_message", "values_en": { "title": "Welcome", "body": "Welcome to our app!" }, "values_ar": { "title": "أهلاً بك", "body": "أهلاً بك في تطبيقنا!" } }' "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/"

    Example Request (PATCH):

    bash curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "values_en": { "title": "Welcome Back", "body": "Welcome back to our app!" } }' "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/"

docs.title: Delete a UI String
docs.text:
• DELETE /api/strings/{key}/

    Deletes a UI string.

    Example Request:

    bash curl -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/"

docs.title: Validation Rules
docs.text:
The following validation rules apply when creating or updating UI strings:

  • key: A unique string used to identify the UI string. This field is required when creating a new string and cannot be changed after creation.
  • values_en: A JSON object containing the English translations. This field is required, and its keys define the structure that values_ar must follow.
  • values_ar: A JSON object containing the Arabic translations. This field is optional and can be null or an empty JSON object ({}). If values_ar is provided and is not empty, it must contain the exact same set of keys as values_en.

docs.title: Gallery System Configuration
docs.text: The gallery system's integration with the main application can be configured via the Global Settings in the admin panel. These settings allow administrators to control the gallery's behavior without requiring code changes.

docs.title: Configuration Fields
docs.text: Setting Description gallery_api_url The base URL for the external Gallery API. This can be changed to point to different environments (e.g., staging or production). gallery_api_timeout The time in seconds the application will wait for a response from the Gallery API before timing out. enable_gallery_system A master switch to completely enable or disable all gallery-related features. If disabled, no galleries will be created, and no API calls will be made. auto_create_trip_gallery If enabled, a new gallery will be automatically created whenever a trip is approved. If disabled, galleries must be created manually. allow_manual_gallery_creation This setting controls whether clients should show UI for manually creating galleries. The API does not enforce this, but clients should respect this flag.

docs.title: HERE Maps Integration
docs.text: This document outlines the configuration and API endpoints for the HERE Maps reverse geocoding feature.

docs.title: Admin Configuration
docs.text:
The HERE Maps integration is configured through the Global Settings in the Django Admin interface. The following fields are available:

  • Here Maps Enabled: Master switch to enable or disable the entire HERE Maps feature.
  • Here Maps Api Key: Your HERE Maps API key.
  • Here Maps Api Base Url: The base URL for the HERE Maps reverse geocoding API.
  • Here Maps Selected Fields: A JSON list of fields to be returned by the reverse geocoding endpoint (e.g., ["city", "district"]).
  • Here Maps Max Fields: The maximum number of fields to display in the formatted area string.
  • Here Maps Available Fields: A JSON object defining the available fields and their display names (e.g., {"city": "City", "district": "District"}).
  • Here Maps Cache Duration: The duration, in days, for which geocoding results are cached in the database.
  • Here Maps Request Timeout: The timeout, in seconds, for requests to the HERE Maps API.

docs.title: Get HERE Maps Configuration
docs.text:
This public endpoint provides the necessary configuration for the frontend to interact with the HERE Maps feature.

  • Endpoint: GET /api/settings/here-maps-config/
  • Authentication: None
  • Response: json { "enabled": true, "selectedFields": ["district", "city"], "maxFields": 2, "availableFields": [ {"name": "title", "displayName": "Place Name"}, {"name": "district", "displayName": "District"}, {"name": "city", "displayName": "City"} ] }

docs.title: Reverse Geocode Coordinates
docs.text:
This endpoint takes a latitude and longitude and returns a formatted area string based on the configured selectedFields and maxFields.

  • Endpoint: POST /api/geocoding/reverse/
  • Authentication: Required
  • Request Body: json { "latitude": 24.4539, "longitude": 54.3773 }
  • Responses:
    • 200 OK: json { "success": true, "area": "Al Ain, Abu Dhabi", "fields": { "district": "Al Ain", "city": "Abu Dhabi" }, "cached": false }
    • 400 Bad Request: If latitude or longitude are missing or invalid.
    • 401 Unauthorized: If the user is not authenticated.
    • 500 Internal Server Error: If there is an error communicating with the HERE Maps API.

docs.title: Digital Logbook
docs.text: The digital logbook allows members to track their progress and have their skills verified by trip leads.

docs.title: Create a Logbook Entry
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/{id}/logbook-entries
    • Creates a new logbook entry for a trip.
    • Requires CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES or CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER permission.

docs.title: View Logbook Entries for a Trip
docs.text:
• GET /api/trips/{id}/viewlogbooks
    • Retrieves a list of members checked in to a trip, along with their associated logbook entry.

docs.title: View Logbook Entries for a Member
docs.text:
• GET /api/members/{id}/logbookentries
    • Retrieves a list of logbook entries for a specific member.

docs.title: List Logbook Skills
docs.text:
• GET /api/logbookskills
    • Retrieves a list of all available logbook skills.
    • The count_requirement field indicates the minimum number of sign-offs required for a skill.
    • The category field is an object containing the ID and name of the skill category.
    • Skills can be filtered by category using the category query parameter (e.g., /api/logbookskills?category=1).

docs.title: Logbook Entry Permissions
docs.text: Creating, updating, and deleting logbook entries is governed by a detailed permission system. The rules are as follows:

docs.title: Members Creating Entries for Themselves
docs.text:
• A member cannot create, update, or delete a logbook entry for themselves.
  • Exception: A member with the CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER permission can create, update, or delete an entry for themselves, provided they are registered for the trip.

docs.title: Members Creating Entries for Other Members
docs.text:
• Trip Lead or Deputy Lead: A trip lead or deputy lead can create, update, or delete a logbook entry for another member, provided that the other member is registered for the trip. The lead/deputy lead does not need to be registered themselves.
  • Superuser (CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER): A member with this permission can create, update, or delete a logbook entry for another member, provided that the other member is registered for the trip.
  • Regular Member (with CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES permission): A regular member can create, update, or delete a logbook entry for another member if all of the following conditions are met:
  • The acting member is registered for the trip.
  • The other member is registered for the trip.
  • The acting member has the CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES permission that applies to the trip's level.

docs.title: Skill Sign-Off Validation (when skills_verified are included in the request)
docs.text:
A user can sign off on skills for another user if any of the following are true:

  • They are the Trip Lead or Deputy Lead for the associated trip.
  • They have the SIGN_LOGBOOK_SKILLS permission AND are registered for the associated trip themselves.
  • They have the CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER permission (this permission bypasses all other skill sign-off checks).

If a user has permission to create or update a logbook entry but lacks the required skill sign-off permissions, the entire request will be denied if it includes skills_verified.

docs.title: Maintenance Mode
docs.text: Occasionally, the AD4x4 API may need to be taken offline for maintenance. When this happens, the API will be put into maintenance mode, and all API requests will receive a 503 Service Unavailable response.

docs.title: Client-Side Handling
docs.text:
Client applications should be designed to handle this response gracefully. When a 503 response is received, the client should:

  • Inform the user: Display a message to the user indicating that the application is temporarily unavailable due to maintenance.
  • Avoid retrying immediately: Do not immediately retry the request, as this will only add to the server load. Instead, wait a reasonable amount of time before attempting to connect again.

docs.title: Meeting Points
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoints for managing meeting points.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Meeting points are predefined locations where trip participants can gather. The API provides endpoints for creating, viewing, updating, and deleting these points.

docs.title: List Meeting Points
docs.text:
• GET /api/meetingpoints/
    • Retrieves a list of all available meeting points.

docs.title: Retrieve a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• GET /api/meetingpoints/{id}/
    • Retrieves the details of a single meeting point.

docs.title: Create a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• POST /api/meetingpoints/
    • Creates a new meeting point. Requires the CREATE_MEETING_POINTS permission.
    • Request Body: json { "name": "Al Faya", "lat": 24.733, "lon": 55.766, "link": "https://goo.gl/maps/...", "area": "AUH" } Note: The area field can be one of DXB, NOR, AUH, AAN, or LIW.

docs.title: Update a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/meetingpoints/{id}/
    • Updates an existing meeting point. Requires the EDIT_MEETING_POINTS permission.
    • The request body should contain the fields to be updated.

docs.title: Delete a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• DELETE /api/meetingpoints/{id}/
    • Deletes a meeting point. Requires the DELETE_MEETING_POINTS permission.

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
This document outlines the API endpoints for member management, including searching for members, retrieving member profiles, and managing member information.

For authentication and registration details, please refer to the Authentication and Profiles document.

docs.title: Member List
docs.text:
You can retrieve a list of members using the standard ViewSet endpoint.

GET /api/members/

Query Parameters: - car_brand, car_year, trip_count, phone, level__numeric_level, level__name, email, first_name, last_name, nationality, city - Filter by various member attributes - page - Page number (default: 1) - page_size - Number of results per page (default: 20, max: 500)

Success Response:

{
  "count": 100,
  "next": "http://api.example.com/api/members/?page=2",
  "previous": null,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "username": "testuser",
      "firstName": "Test",
      "lastName": "User",
      "level": "Newbie",
      "tripCount": 5,
      "carBrand": "Toyota",
      "carModel": "Land Cruiser",
      "carColor": "White",
      "carImage": null,
      "paidMember": true
    }
  ]
}

Note: Contact information (email, phone) is only visible to users with the VIEW_CONTACT_INFO permission or when viewing their own profile.

docs.title: Search Members
docs.text:
Search for members by username, first name, or last name. This is useful for finding members when adding trip participants, looking up member profiles, or searching for trip leads.

GET /api/members/search/

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Required Description query string Yes Search term - must be at least 3 characters. Matches against username, first name, and last name (case-insensitive partial match) level integer No Level ID for filtering to include only members at a specific level min_level integer No Minimum level ID for filtering to include only members at this level or higher (inclusive) max_level integer No Maximum level ID for filtering to include only members at this level or lower (inclusive) page integer No Page number (default: 1) page_size integer No Number of results per page (default: 20, max: 500)

Level Filtering Examples:

# Search for Newbies (level ID 10)
GET /api/members/search/?query=john&level=10

# Search for members Newbie (10) and up to Intermediate (100) inclusive
GET /api/members/search/?query=john&max_level=100

# Search for members Intermediate (100) and higher inclusive
GET /api/members/search/?query=john&min_level=100

Request Example:

# Basic search
curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/members/search/?query=john&page=1&page_size=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

# Search for Newbies only
curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/members/search/?query=john&level=10&page=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

# Search for members Newbie to Intermediate inclusive
curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/members/search/?query=john&max_level=100&page=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Success Response (200 OK):

{
  "count": 42,
  "next": "http://api.example.com/api/members/search/?query=john&page=2",
  "previous": null,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "username": "johndoe",
      "firstName": "John",
      "lastName": "Doe",
      "level": "Marshall",
      "tripCount": 25,
      "carBrand": "Toyota",
      "carModel": "Land Cruiser",
      "carColor": "White",
      "carImage": null,
      "paidMember": true
    }
  ]
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request - Missing query):

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "query_parameter_required"
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request - Query too short):

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "query_too_short"
}

Error Response (401 Unauthorized):

{
  "detail": "Authentication credentials were not provided."
}

Error Response (403 Forbidden):

{
  "detail": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
}

Notes: - The search is case-insensitive and performs partial matching (contains) - Query must be at least 3 characters long - Results are ordered by trip_count (descending), then by id (ascending) - Results are paginated using standard pagination - Matches across username, first_name, and last_name fields using OR logic - Results can be filtered by level using level, min_level, or max_level parameters - Contact information (email, phone) is only visible to users with the VIEW_CONTACT_INFO permission or when viewing their own profile - Permission Required: Users must have the SEARCH_MEMBERS permission to use this endpoint. By default, this is granted to Newbie level and above. ANIT members cannot use this endpoint.

Use Cases: - Finding members when adding trip participants - Looking up member profiles - Searching for trip leads or coordinators - Member directory lookup functionality

docs.title: Member Profile Details
docs.text:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific member.

GET /api/members/{id}/

Success Response:

{

docs.title: Update Member Profile
docs.text:
Update a member's profile. Users can only update their own profiles unless they are an administrator.

PATCH /api/members/{id}/

Request Body: The request body should contain the fields to be updated. Note that some fields like username, email, and level are read-only.

Success Response: A successful update will return a 200 OK status code and the updated profile data.

docs.title: Lead Search
docs.text:
Search for members who have permission to lead trips.

GET /api/members/leadsearch/

Query Parameters: - search - Search term (searches in username, first name, last name) - level - Level ID for filtering to include only members that have permission to lead for a given level

Success Response:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "username": "johndoe",
    "firstName": "John",
    "lastName": "Doe",
    "level": "Marshall",

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: This document outlines the different types of push and email notifications sent by the backend.

docs.title: Registering for Push Notifications
docs.text:
To receive push notifications, the client application must register the device's FCM token with the backend. This is done by making a POST request to the /api/device/fcm/ endpoint.

POST /api/device/fcm/

Request Body:

{
    "registrationId": "your-fcm-token",
    "type": "ios"
}

The type can be ios, android, or web.

For more information on Firebase Cloud Messaging, please refer to the official documentation.

docs.title: Trips
docs.text:
• New Trip Notification: Sent when a new trip is created.
  • Trip Approval Notification: Sent when a trip is approved or rejected.
  • Accepted from Waitlist: Sent to a member when they are moved from the waitlist to the registered list for a trip.
  • Removed from Trip Registered List: Sent to a member when they are removed from the registered list for a trip.
  • Removed from Trip Waitlist: Sent to a member when they are removed from the waitlist for a trip.
  • New Trip Comment: Sent when a new comment is added to a trip. This is used for the real-time chat feature.

docs.title: Upgrade Requests
docs.text:
• Upgrade Request Handled: Sent to a member when their upgrade request has been handled (approved or rejected).
  • Upgrade Request Created: Sent to the marshals when a new upgrade request is created.
  • Upgrade Request Reminder: A periodic reminder sent to the marshals about open upgrade requests.

docs.title: Club News
docs.text: • Club-Wide News: Sent to all members when a new club news item is published.

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text: • Feedback Notification: Sent to the administrators when a member submits feedback.

docs.title: NotificationType Enum Values
docs.text:
The type field in the notification object will contain one of the following enum values:

Value Description NEW_TRIP A new trip has been created. TRIP_APPR A trip has been approved or rejected. WAIT_ACC A user has been accepted from the waitlist. UPG_REQ_HAN An upgrade request has been handled. UPG_REQ_CRE A new upgrade request has been created. UPG_REQ_REM A reminder for an open upgrade request. CLUB_NEWS A new club news item has been published. REM_FROM_TRIP_REG A user has been removed from a trip's registered list. REM_FROM_TRIP_WAIT A user has been removed from a trip's waitlist.

docs.title: Notification History
docs.text:
A log of all notifications sent to a member is stored in the database. This allows the client application to display a history of notifications to the user.

GET /api/notifications/

The endpoint returns a paginated list of the 20 most recent notifications for the authenticated user. Each notification object in the response now includes an is_read boolean field, which indicates whether the notification has been read by the user.

docs.title: Marking Notifications as Read
docs.text:
To mark one or more notifications as read, the client can make a POST request to the /api/notifications/mark-as-read/ endpoint.

POST /api/notifications/mark-as-read/

Request Body:

{
    "notificationIds": [1, 2, 3]
}

The notificationIds field should contain a list of notification IDs to be marked as read. The endpoint will return a 204 No Content response on success.

docs.title: Notification Purging
docs.text: To prevent the notification log from growing indefinitely, a periodic background task runs daily to purge old notifications. Any notification logs older than 60 days are automatically deleted from the database.

docs.title: Permissions, Groups, and Levels
docs.text: This document provides a comprehensive overview of the permissions system used in the API. It details the different user groups, experience levels, and the specific actions each group is permitted to perform by default.

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text:
The permissions system is built on three main concepts:

  • Groups: Users are assigned to one or more groups, which determine their general role and permissions.
  • Levels: Levels represent a user's experience or seniority within the club (e.g., Newbie, Intermediate, Marshal). Some permissions are restricted to certain levels.
  • Actions: These are specific permissions that grant the ability to perform a particular operation via the API (e.g., CREATE_TRIP, APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ).

Permissions are granted to groups, and can optionally be restricted to apply only to certain levels.

docs.title: Fetching User Permissions
docs.text:
To get the permissions for a specific user, you can retrieve their profile from the /api/members/{id}/ endpoint. The user's permissions are included in the permissions array in the response.

GET /api/members/{id}/

Example Response Snippet:

{
    "id": 1,
    "username": "testuser",
    ...
    "permissions": [
        "CREATE_TRIP",
        "VIEW_CONTACT_INFO"
    ],
    ...
}

docs.title: Groups and Levels
docs.text:
The following table lists the default groups and their corresponding experience levels:

Group Level Numeric Level Notes Newbies Newbie 10 Default for new users Intermediates Intermediate 100 Advanced Advance 200 Experts Expert 300 Disabled by default Explorers Explorer 400 Marshals Marshal 600 Board members Board member 800 Non-level Groups Trip managers N/A N/A Meeting point managers N/A N/A Media managers N/A N/A Upgrade request managers N/A N/A Site admins N/A N/A Super-users with all permissions

docs.title: Default Permissions by Group
docs.text: Here is a breakdown of the default permissions assigned to each group.

docs.title: Newbies
docs.text: • Can search for members in the member directory.

docs.title: Explorers
docs.text:
• Can create trips that require approval for the "Newbie" level.
  • Can create trips that do not require approval for "Intermediate" level and above.
  • Can create meeting points.
  • Can view contact information of other members.
  • Can create logbook entries and sign off on skills for trips they lead or support

docs.title: Marshals
docs.text:
• Can create trips without requiring approval.
  • Can view, vote on, and comment on upgrade requests.

docs.title: Board Members
docs.text:
• Can view, vote on, and comment on upgrade requests.
  • Can approve upgrade requests.
  • Can override the global waitlist setting for trips.

docs.title: Upgrade Request Managers
docs.text:
• Can view, vote on, comment on, edit, and delete upgrade requests.
  • Can delete comments on upgrade requests.

docs.title: Trip Managers
docs.text:
• Can create, edit, approve, and delete trips.
  • Can edit trip registrations and delete trip comments.
  • Can override the global waitlist setting for trips.
  • Have superuser permissions for creating logbook entries.

docs.title: Media Managers
docs.text: • Can edit trip media.

docs.title: Meeting Point Managers
docs.text: • Can create, edit, and delete meeting points.

docs.title: Site Admins
docs.text: • Have all permissions.

docs.title: Full List of Permissions (Actions)
docs.text:
The following table lists all possible actions in the system.

Action Description CREATE_TRIP Create Trip CREATE_TRIP_WITH_APPROVAL Create Trip With Approval CREATE_TRIP_REPORT Create Trip Report APPROVE_TRIP Approve Trip OVERRIDE_WAITLIST_SETTING Override Global Waitlist Setting BYPASS_LEVEL_REQ Bypass Level Requirements for Trip EDIT_TRIPS Edit Trips EDIT_TRIP_MEDIA Edit Trip Media EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS Edit Trip Registrations DELETE_TRIPS Delete Trips DELETE_TRIP_COMMENTS Delete Trip Comments CREATE_MEETING_POINTS Create Meeting Points EDIT_MEETING_POINTS Edit Meeting Points DELETE_MEETING_POINTS Delete Meeting Points CREATE_UPGRADE_REQ_FOR_SELF Create Upgrade Request For Self CREATE_UPGRADE_REQ_FOR_OTHERS Create Upgrade Request For Others EDIT_UPGRADE_REQ Edit Upgrade Request APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ Approve Upgrade Request DELETE_UPGRADE_REQ Delete Upgrade Request VIEW_UPGRADE_REQ View Upgrade Request (ALL levels) VOTE_UPGRADE_REQ Vote Upgrade Request CREATE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ Comment Upgrade Request DELETE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ Delete Comment Upgrade Request EDIT_MEMBERSHIP_PAYMENTS Edit Membership Payments CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES Create Logbook Entries SIGN_LOGBOOK_SKILLS Sign Logbook Skills CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER Create Logbook Entries (superuser bypass) ACCESS_MARSHAL_PANEL Access Marshal Panel VIEW_CONTACT_INFO View Contact Info SEARCH_MEMBERS Search Members EDIT_UI_STRINGS Edit UI Strings EDIT_GLOBAL_SETTINGS Edit Global Settings

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text: To ensure the stability and reliability of the AD4x4 API, we have implemented rate limiting. This means that each client is limited to a certain number of requests per minute.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The rate limiting is configured in the Nginx default.conf.template file. The current limit is set to 100 requests per minute per IP address.

docs.title: HTTP 429 Response
docs.text:
If you exceed the rate limit, the API will respond with an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests status code. When you receive this response, you should:

  • Stop sending requests: Do not send any more requests until the rate limit window has reset.
  • Inform the user: Display a message to the user indicating that they have exceeded the rate limit and should try again later.
  • Implement backoff: Consider implementing an exponential backoff strategy to gradually reduce the rate of your requests.

docs.title: Swagger UI
docs.text:
Our API documentation is powered by Swagger, which provides an interactive way to explore and test the API. You can access the Swagger UI at the following URL:

https://ap.ad4x4.com/docs/swagger-ui/

docs.title: Authorizing with a Bearer Token
docs.text:
To test the protected endpoints in the Swagger UI, you'll need to obtain a bearer token and authorize your requests. Here's how to do it:

  1. Log in to the API: Send a POST request to the /api/auth/login/ endpoint with your username and password. The response will contain an access token.

  2. Authorize in Swagger:

    • Click the "Authorize" button at the top-right of the Swagger page.
    • In the dialog that appears, enter the word Bearer followed by a space and then the access token you received in the previous step. For example: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...
    • Click "Authorize" to save the token.

Once you've authorized, you can make requests to any of the protected endpoints in the Swagger UI.

docs.title: Trips
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoint for searching trips. For general trip management, please refer to the Trips document.

docs.title: Search Trips
docs.text:
Search for trips by title, with optional filters for level, date ranges, meeting point, and area. This endpoint is useful for finding specific trips, browsing trip history, or discovering trip activities.

Endpoint: GET /api/trips/search/

Authentication: Required (Bearer token) Permission Required: Users must have SEARCH_TRIPS permission to access this endpoint.

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description query string Yes Search term - must be at least 3 characters. Matches against trip title (case-insensitive partial match) level integer No Trip level ID for filtering to include only trips at a specific level min_level integer No Minimum level numeric value for filtering to include only trips at this level or higher (inclusive) max_level integer No Maximum level numeric value for filtering to include only trips at this level or lower (inclusive) start_date_min date (ISO 8601) No Filter for trips starting from this date (inclusive) start_date_max date (ISO 8601) No Filter for trips starting until this date (inclusive) end_date_min date (ISO 8601) No Filter for trips ending from this date (inclusive) end_date_max date (ISO 8601) No Filter for trips ending until this date (inclusive) meeting_point integer No Filter for trips at a specific meeting point (exact match by ID) area string No Filter for trips in a specific area page integer No Page number (default: 1) page_size integer No Number of results per page (default: 20, max: 500)

docs.title: Request Examples
docs.text:
Basic search:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search/?query=fun" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Search with level filter:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search/?query=adventure&level=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Search with date range:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search/?query=expedition&start_date_min=2024-01-01&end_date_max=2024-12-31" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Search by meeting point:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search/?query=beach&meeting_point=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Search by area:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search/?query=desert&area=DUBAI" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Paginated search:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search/?query=trip&page=1&page_size=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

docs.title: Success Response (200 OK)
docs.text:
{
  "count": 42,
  "next": "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search/?query=adventure&page=2",
  "previous": null,

    {

docs.title: Error Responses
docs.text:
Error Response (400 Bad Request - Missing query):

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "query_parameter_required"
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request - Query too short):

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "query_too_short"
}

Error Response (403 Forbidden):

  "detail": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The search is case-insensitive and performs partial matching (contains) on trip titles
  • Query must be at least 3 characters long
  • Results are ordered by start_time (descending), then by id (ascending)
  • Results are paginated using standard pagination (20 items per page by default)
  • Level filtering: Use level for exact level match, or min_level/max_level for range filtering
  • Example: ?level=10 returns only Newbie trips
  • Example: ?min_level=100 returns Intermediate and higher level trips
  • Example: ?max_level=100 returns Newbie and Intermediate level trips
  • Date filtering: Use start_date_min/max and end_date_min/max to filter by date ranges
  • Trips that have ended (cut_off is in the past) are automatically excluded from results
  • If end_date_max is set without end_date_min, only trips ending on or before that date are included
  • Similarly for start dates
  • Meeting point filtering: Use meeting_point to filter by exact meeting point ID
  • Area filtering: Use area to filter by meeting point area code
  • Permission Required: Users must have SEARCH_TRIPS permission. By default, this is granted to Newbie level and above.
  • Performance Note: This endpoint searches trip titles efficiently. Searching by trip lead's user info (username, first name, last name) requires additional database joins and can be slower with many trips. Use title-based search for better performance.
  • User-specific information: For authenticated users, the response includes trip-specific registration status:
  • isRegistered: Whether the authenticated user is registered for this trip
  • isWaitlisted: Whether the authenticated user is on the waitlist for this trip
  • waitlistCount: Current number of users on the waitlist
  • registeredCount: Current number of users registered for this trip

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Finding specific trips by title search
  • Browsing available trips for a specific level (e.g., Newbie trips only)
  • Discovering trip activities by date range
  • Finding trips at specific meeting points
  • Exploring trips in specific geographic areas
  • Checking trip history for a user or level
  • Building trip calendars or schedules

docs.title: Trips
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoints for managing trips, including creating, viewing, registering, and managing participants.

docs.title: Trip Lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Creation: A trip is created via a POST request. Depending on the creator's permissions, it may be automatically approved or require manual approval.
  2. Approval: Trips requiring approval must be approved by a user with the appropriate permissions before they become visible to regular members.
  3. Registration: Once a trip is approved, members can register for it until the cut_off time is reached or the capacity is filled.
  4. Waitlist: If a trip is full and allow_waitlist is enabled, members can join the waitlist. They will be automatically moved to the registered list if a spot becomes available.
  5. Check-in/Check-out: The trip lead or a deputy can check members in and out of the trip.

docs.title: List and Retrieve Trips
docs.text:
• GET /api/trips/
    • Retrieves a list of all approved trips.
  • GET /api/trips/{id}/
    • Retrieves the full details of a single trip, including registered members and the waitlist.

docs.title: Create a Trip
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/

    • Creates a new trip. The approval_status will be set based on the user's permissions.
    • Request Body: See the CreateTripSerializer for details. Key fields include:
      • lead (Member ID)
      • level (Level ID)
      • title
      • start_time
      • end_time
      • cut_off
      • capacity
      • meeting_point (MeetingPoint ID)

    Note: While the serializer and database use snake_case for field names (e.g., start_time), the API expects camelCase in the request body (e.g., startTime).

docs.title: Update a Trip
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/trips/{id}/
    • Updates an existing trip.
    • Restrictions:
      • A configurable cutoff time (in minutes before the trip's start_time) determines when editing is restricted. The default is 0 minutes, meaning editing is disabled once the trip starts.
      • Before the cutoff time: The trip's lead and users with the EDIT_TRIPS permission can edit the trip.
      • After the cutoff time: Only users with the EDIT_TRIPS permission can edit the trip.
      • Superusers are exempt from all restrictions.
    • Request Body: See the UpdateTripSerializer for a list of editable fields.

docs.title: Delete a Trip
docs.text:
• DELETE /api/trips/{id}/
    • Deletes a trip. This is a soft-delete, meaning the trip's approval_status is set to DELETED.
    • Restrictions:
      • A configurable cutoff time (in minutes before the trip's start_time) determines when deleting is restricted. The default is 0 minutes, meaning deleting is disabled once the trip starts.
      • Before the cutoff time: The trip's lead and users with the DELETE_TRIPS permission can delete the trip.
      • After the cutoff time: Only users with the DELETE_TRIPS permission can delete the trip.
      • Superusers are exempt from all restrictions.

docs.title: Approve a Trip
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/{id}/approve/
    • Approves a trip that is pending approval. Requires the APPROVE_TRIP permission.

docs.title: Registration
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/{id}/register/
    • Registers the authenticated user for the trip.
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/waitlist/
    • Adds the authenticated user to the waitlist if the trip is full.
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/unregister/
    • Cancels the authenticated user's registration for the trip (from either the registered list or the waitlist).

docs.title: Participant Management
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/{id}/addfromwaitlist/
    • Manually moves a member from the waitlist to the registered list. Requires EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS permission or being the trip lead/deputy.
    • Request Body: {"member": <member_id>}
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/removemember/
    • Removes a member from the trip (from either the registered list or the waitlist). Requires EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS permission or being the trip lead/deputy.
    • Request Body: {"member": <member_id>, "reason": "..."}
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/checkin/
    • Checks in one or more members to the trip.
    • Request Body: {"members": [<member_id_1>, <member_id_2>]}
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/checkout/
    • Checks out one or more members from the trip.
    • Request Body: {"members": [<member_id_1>, <member_id_2>]}

docs.title: Member-Specific Trip Endpoints
docs.text: These endpoints provide trip information tailored to a specific member.

docs.title: Member Trip Counts
docs.text:
• GET /api/members/{id}/tripcounts/
    • Retrieves a summary of a member's completed trips, grouped by trip level.

    • Note: This endpoint only includes trips with an APPROVED status where the member was successfully checked in.

docs.title: Member Trip History
docs.text:
• GET /api/members/{id}/triphistory/
    • Retrieves a paginated history of a member's trips.

    • Note: This endpoint only includes trips with an APPROVED status.

See also the Digital Logbook page for information on how to manage logbook entries for a trip.

docs.title: Upgrade Requests
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoints for managing level upgrade requests.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Members can request to be upgraded to a higher level. This process involves creating a request, which is then reviewed and voted on by authorized members (e.g., Marshals, Board Members).

docs.title: List and Retrieve Upgrade Requests
docs.text:
• GET /api/upgraderequests/
    • Retrieves a list of upgrade requests. Requires VIEW_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
  • GET /api/upgraderequests/{id}/
    • Retrieves the details of a single upgrade request.

docs.title: Get Member Upgrade Eligibility
docs.text:
• GET /api/members/{id}/upgradeeligibility
    • Retrieves a detailed report on a member's eligibility for an upgrade to the next potential level. This report includes a breakdown of met/unmet requirements based on minimum trips at the current level and required logbook skills for the next level.
    • Authorization:
      • A member can view their own eligibility (when {id} matches request.user.id).
      • Members with the view_upgrade_req permission can view the eligibility of any member.
    • Response Structure (Example): json { "member_id": 1, "member_username": "testuser", "current_level": { "id": 1, "name": "Beginner", "numeric_level": 1 }, "next_potential_level": { "id": 2, "name": "Intermediate", "numeric_level": 2 }, "upgrade_requirements": [ { "type": "min_trips", "name": "Minimum trips for current level", "required_value": 5, "current_value": 3, "met": false, "description": "You need 5 trips at your current level (completed at this level).", "recent_trips_at_level": [ { "trip_id": 10, "title": "Desert Crossing", "start_time": "2025-11-15T09:00:00Z", "lead": {"id": 1, "username": "leader1"}, "level": {"id": 1, "name": "Beginner", "numeric_level": 1} }, { "trip_id": 9, "title": "Mountain Trail", "start_time": "2025-10-20T08:00:00Z", "lead": {"id": 2, "username": "leader2"}, "level": {"id": 1, "name": "Beginner", "numeric_level": 1} } ] }, { "type": "logbook_skill", "skill_id": 101, "skill_name": "Basic Recovery", "required_count": 2, "current_count": 1, "met": false, "description": "Complete 'Basic Recovery' 2 times.", "signatures": [ { "trip_id": 15, "signed_by": {"id": 5, "username": "verifier_user"}, "signed_date": "2025-12-01T10:30:00Z" } ] }, { "type": "logbook_skill", "skill_id": 102, "skill_name": "Tyre Changing", "required_count": 1, "current_count": 1, "met": true, "description": "Complete 'Tyre Changing' 1 time.", "signatures": [ { "trip_id": 12, "signed_by": {"id": 6, "username": "another_verifier"}, "signed_date": "2025-11-25T14:00:00Z" } ] } ], "is_eligible_for_upgrade": false }

docs.title: Create an Upgrade Request
docs.text:
• POST /api/upgraderequests/

    • Creates a new upgrade request.
    • Eligibility Check: Before creation, the system checks if the applicant is eligible for an upgrade based on minimum trips at their current level and required logbook skills for the target level. If the applicant is not eligible, or is already at the highest available level, the request will be rejected with a 400 Bad Request status and a detailed error message listing unmet requirements.
    • Request Body: See the CreateUpgradeRequestSerializer for details. Key fields include:
      • applicant (Member ID of the person being nominated for upgrade)
      • target_level (Level ID)
      • applicant_reason (Text description)
      • nominated_voters (List of Member IDs)

    Note: While the serializer and database use snake_case for field names (e.g., target_level), the API expects camelCase in the request body (e.g., targetLevel).

docs.title: Update an Upgrade Request
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/upgraderequests/{id}/
    • Updates an existing upgrade request. Requires EDIT_UPGRADE_REQ permission.

docs.title: Voting and Approval
docs.text:
• POST /api/upgraderequests/{id}/vote/
    • Casts a vote on an upgrade request. Requires VOTE_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
    • Request Body: {"vote": "Y"} (or "N" for No, "D" for Defer)
  • POST /api/upgraderequests/{id}/approve/
    • Approves an upgrade request. Requires APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
  • POST /api/upgraderequests/{id}/decline/
    • Declines an upgrade request. Requires APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
    • Request Body: {"verdict_reason": "..."}

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
• GET /api/upgraderequests/{id}/comments/
    • Retrieves all comments for a specific upgrade request.
  • POST /api/upgraderequestcomments/
    • Adds a new comment to an upgrade request. Requires CREATE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
    • Request Body: {"upgrade_request": <request_id>, "text": "..."}
  • DELETE /api/upgraderequestcomments/{id}/
    • Deletes a comment. Requires DELETE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
